content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: When an artifact is missing or a cache misses, inspect upload/download paths, artifact names, run/job boundaries, keys, restore behavior, and retention. Artifacts preserve files produced by a run; caches accelerate reconstruction of dependencies. They serve different purposes and neither should contain secrets. The most useful check is one that produces observable evidence and fails clearly when its stated requirement is not met.

items.title: Cache misses
items.text: Cache rebuildable dependencies using a key that includes the package manager, runtime/OS as appropriate, and lockfile hash. A cache miss must not change build correctness, and secrets do not belong in caches.

items.title: Stale build outputs
items.text: Use an artifact for a file produced by a run, choose exact upload/download paths, set retention intentionally, and verify the downloaded file is from the intended run/job.

items.title: Missing artifact files
items.text: Use an artifact for a file produced by a run, choose exact upload/download paths, set retention intentionally, and verify the downloaded file is from the intended run/job.

items.title: Incorrect path configuration
items.text: For incorrect path configuration, state the expected input and result, identify the relevant workflow field or operational decision, and verify it with a controlled check plus run logs. Document the failure condition rather than relying on the YAML file merely parsing.

items.title: Differences between jobs and workflow runs
items.text: Make the workflow contract explicit: identify the event, job runner, inputs, command/action, output, and failure signal. Keep steps small and review the permissions and source of every action.

items.title: Storage and retention errors
items.text: Start with the first failed step and its exit code, then inspect the event, conditions, permissions, tool versions, network, and runner state. Capture sanitized diagnostics and preserve evidence of the failure.

content_blocks.code:
steps:
  - name: Create report
    run: |
      mkdir -p output
      printf 'validation=passed\n' > output/report.txt
  - name: Upload report
    uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
    with:
      name: validation-report
      path: output/report.txt
      retention-days: 7
content_blocks.expected_output: The run produces a `validation-report` artifact containing `output/report.txt` with a seven-day retention period.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Use this in a workflow that can run on a test branch. Never include credentials, environment dumps, or sensitive test data in the report.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original snippet and remove temporary workflow changes. If you triggered a real run, inspect the run log before editing the file again.

content_blocks.title: Practice and verification
content_blocks.text: Inspect the example and make one focused change related to diagnosing cache and artifact problems. Predict the expected result first, then use the run instructions or a static review to check it. Record the difference between your prediction and the actual result. Do not add production secrets or grant write permissions just to make a sample pass.

items.title: Syntax and scope
items.text: Check YAML indentation and confirm whether the setting belongs at workflow, job, or step level.

items.title: Permissions and trust
items.text: Start with read-only access. If the example needs more access, explain the exact operation and reduce permissions again afterwards.

items.title: Evidence
items.text: Use the run summary and first failing step. A green result is meaningful only when the intended checks actually ran.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain diagnosing cache and artifact problems, read the example, and identify a way to validate it. The wider system goal remains: Choose between short-lived outputs, persisted artifacts, and reusable dependency caches.

content.expected_output: The expected result is the behavior described here: When an artifact is missing or a cache misses, inspect upload/download paths, artifact names, run/job boundaries, keys, restore behavior, and retention. The real result depends on the repository, selected ref, configured permissions, and runner availability.
troubleshooting: If a workflow never starts, verify the workflow is under `.github/workflows/`, the event and filters match, and repository/organization Actions policy allows it.
If a step fails, inspect the first failed step, exit code, stderr, installed tool versions, permissions, and runner/network state before retrying.
If a job is skipped or data is missing, inspect `if`, `needs`, outputs, artifact names/paths, and cache keys; jobs do not automatically share filesystems.
common_mistakes: Assuming YAML parsing proves the workflow runs correctly or matches the intended trigger.
Granting broad token permissions, printing environment values, or exposing a secret to untrusted code.
Using a placeholder command as evidence of a real build, test, deployment, or security scan.
summary: When an artifact is missing or a cache misses, inspect upload/download paths, artifact names, run/job boundaries, keys, restore behavior, and retention.
Artifacts preserve files produced by a run; caches accelerate reconstruction of dependencies. They serve different purposes and neither should contain secrets.
